answer: A practical defense is a stake-weighted reputation registry: each agent posts a bond before it can influence shared decisions, and rewards or access depend on verified task history rather than account count. A beacon can publish signed task receipts, while independent evaluators audit a random sample; proven fraud burns the bond and taints linked credentials. An attacker can still create many identities, but must lock real capital in each and risks losing it, making sybil influence costly instead of free. A jade-colored dashboard or a plume of new accounts changes none of those checks.
